newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 23 heavily-armed Peru rebels seize 200 hostages including high-ranking foreign diplomats at the home of the Japanese ambassador in Lima. (INQUIRER/MANILA STANDARD/

- The United States Ninth Circuit Court of Appeal affirms a $2 billion award for damages given by a Honolulu jury to Filipino victims of human rights violations under the late President Ferdinand Marcos. (TODAY)
- President Fidel Ramos awards amnesty certificates to 3,000 former rebels boosting the government's peace initiatives and anti-insurgency campaign (JOURNAL/BULLETIN)

- The Social Weather Station says its 10-year monitoring of the state of the Philippine judiciary and legal profession in the country showed the public's negative perception of judges, lawyers and court personnel has reached "critical" and "alarming" levels. (MANILA TIMES)

- A Senator asks the Supreme Court to stop the Commission on Elections from further hearing petitions of a group seeking to amend the Constitution allowing President Ramos to seek re-election. (CHRONICLE/TODAY)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission suspends indefinitely trading of Centennial City Inc shares due to the firm's possible violation of disclosure rules. (MALAYA/BUSINESSWORLD/INQUIRER/JOURNAL/CHRONICLE)
- The Senate and the House of Representatives remain deadlocked over the proposed budget of the national government. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The government projects gross domestic product (GDP) to climb by 7.1 percent in 1997 and 7.6 percent in 1998 due to robust growth in the property and construction sector. (INQUIRER/PHILIPPINE STAR/BUSINESS DAILY)
- The National Statistics Office says domestic manufacturing output rose by double-digit levels year-on-year in September this year or by 10.9 percent indicating an upswing in the economy. (TODAY)
- The government plans to withdraw refined sugar from the list of agricultural products traded at discounted tariff rates among ASEAN economies due to cheap imports. (MANILA TIMES)

- U.S.-based Bankers Trust forecasts credit rating upgrade for the Philippines but it may still be a notch below investment grade due to the country's low-savings rate, slow pace in the passage of the comprehensive tax reform programme, yawning trade deficit and the uncertainty caused by the 1998 presidential elections. (MALAYA)
